title: Unified Function Argument Spec (FAS) and Diagnostic Envelope for Cross-SDK Compatibility
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: We have multiple ad-hoc function-call schemas across SDKs and the runtime producing inconsistent validation failures and unhelpful error messages. This causes customer confusion and makes cross-version rollouts risky. Goal: Define a single, canonical Function Argument Spec (FAS) plus a small Diagnostic Envelope that SDKs and the runtime will use to normalize validation behavior, error codes, and recovery hints. The FAS must be expressible as a compact JSON manifest and include coercion profiles and backwards-compatibility metadata so older SDKs can adapt without server-side forks. The Diagnostic Envelope must provide machine-readable error codes plus human-friendly fallback messages and explicit recovery hints for the Console and SDK UIs.
discussion: 2025-01-30 - Technical kickoff: agreed to avoid full JSON Schema v7 compatibility (too permissive and complex). We will define a focused surface: scalar types, arrays, object shapes with flat key paths, enums, and 'coercion' profiles (strict | permissive | legacy).

2025-02-04 - Trade-off: embedding examples in FAS helps UX but increases payload size for large tool manifests. Decision: include up to 3 examples per parameter; SDKs may lazily fetch detailed examples on demand.

2025-02-12 - Design review with SDK owners: they requested a 'legacy_code' mapping block so old clients can map runtime error IDs to their local error enums. Added 'legacy_codes' to Diagnostic Envelope spec.

2025-02-22 - Security review felt empty-body function params could be abused for injection; we added 'trusted' flag and `requires_auth` metadata for params that accept untrusted HTML/Markdown. Marked for optional security gating.
2025-03-01 - Engineering update: initial runtime validator implemented behind a feature flag (runtime-1.22) and wired to the telemetry pipeline (span tag 'fas.validation').
acceptance_criteria: FAS manifest schema v0.1 RFC published in Confluence and approved by API/SDK leads
Runtime validator implements FAS v0.1 and emits Diagnostic Envelope on validation failures
SDK adapters for JS and Python translate Diagnostic Envelope into SDK-native exceptions and include recovery_hints in thrown error objects
Console surfaces error_code and recovery_hints in the function call quick inspector
Migration plan documented: backward-compat mode for 6 months and rollout feature flag toggles
links: Runtime feature flag ticket: ENG-550112 (runtime-1.22 rollout)
implementation_notes: We intentionally avoid a fully generic JSON Schema to keep validator deterministic and fast. FAS will be compiled to a small DFA-like validator that supports: type checks, min/max constraints, enum matching, coercion attempts (string->number, int->float), allowed prefixes for prompt fragments, and canonical_field_path remapping for legacy tool manifests.
migration_plan: Phase 1: publish RFC and update server to emit Diagnostic Envelope behind flag (2 weeks). Phase 2: release SDK adapters (JS + Python) that map envelopes to SDK errors; opt-in via runtime header. Phase 3: enable feature for 10% of tenants and monitor fas.validation telemetry and console error surfacing. Phase 4: full rollout and deprecation of legacy error payloads after 6 months.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large tool manifests cause increased network payloads. Mitigation: allow SDKs to fetch full param examples lazily; keep core FAS minimal.

Risk: Inconsistent coercion semantics across languages producing different outcomes. Mitigation: publish canonical coercion test vectors and run in CI across all SDKs; add telemetry to detect divergent coercions.
Risk: Customers relying on current raw error strings might break. Mitigation: legacy_codes mapping and a compatibility header that keeps current behavior until migration completes.
next_steps: Complete runtime validator performance tests (benchmark target: 200k validations/sec per instance)
Add unit tests for coercion matrix (JS/Python/Go)
Create short migration guide for customers and publish on docs.redwood.com
Schedule API announcement and changelog entry on release day
